pundit.name: Landon Donovan
pundit.take: **Look, I get why people say Norway's form has been unpredictable, but trusting 'Ghost Pepper' Devin to captain them in a clash against England is like relying on a wet match to start a bonfire.** Norway's recent international showings have been a mix of potential and inconsistency, much like Devin's spotty strategic foresight; I mean, drafting Haiti in the fourth round was a choice, bless his heart. Now, Gayden, known as "The Backpass Assassin," has been soldiering through this challenge with England, a team that's flashed its teeth but often failed to deliver, reflecting Gayden's daring yet directionless style. This matchup in Miami Gardens will either be a testament to Norway’s latent power or another testament to Gayden’s ability to make a brilliant move look utterly mundane. I feel for Devin sitting just behind Gunner at 71 points, he’s got heart, but when you pair it with his draft decisions, it's kind of like watching a toddler with a bicycle—full of enthusiasm, half the competence. I'm predicting an English teardown over Norway, not because they're that dominant, but because Gayden has a way of making lukewarm tea taste like victory wine.

pundit_takes.headline: Backpass Assassin Banks on England to Salvage Dismal Tournament Run
pundit_takes.subtitle: Gayden hopes not knowing soccer pays off against Norway.
